title: Ghost effect from Boltzmann theory
reviewed_version: arXiv:2301.09427v3, 18 September 2023, 76 pages; not a comparison of the journal final text
summary: A family of nongrazing short chords in the unit ball disproves the flight-count assertion following the union in (9.17). The failure occurs in the stochastic-cycle derivation underlying the core L-infinity estimate. An intersection, as used in the acquired predecessor preprint, and an inclusive binomial sum restore the required tail scaling. Neither Lemma 9.5's measure estimate nor Theorem 1.2 is disproved.
limitations: Bounded review; not exhaustive proof certification of all 76 pages.
Boundary-layer, elliptic, BV, coercivity and compactness estimates outside the declared inspected steps were not independently established.
Journal text not compared; no proof of absence of later or unpublished corrections.
No author code executed; missing code is not a mathematical defect.
No independent scientific acceptance or human review.

problems.title: The union-defined nongrazing set does not imply the flight count
problems.affected_object: Displayed deterministic derivation, not a demonstrated false final theorem

source_locator.equation: (9.17), sentence following it and use in (9.18)

problems.claim: On t_k<Tcal/epsilon at most floor(C_Omega*Tcal/eta^3)+1 of the velocities belong to the UNION of positive-normal threshold and low-speed sets.
assumptions_verified: Omega is the unit ball, a bounded C-infinity domain in R^3.
Any fixed P>0; any sufficiently small positive epsilon.
Every selected velocity has norm 1/2 and normal component delta>0; no zero or grazing velocity.
x0=x1-4*delta*v1 is strictly interior with norm squared 1-4*delta^2.
eta is positive and less than 1; Tcal can be arbitrarily large; k is any integer at least M+2, including admissible large values in the proof.
problems.check: For delta=min(eta/2,Tcal/(16k),1/8), use v_j=delta*x_j+sqrt(1/4-delta^2)*tau_j. A full chord takes 8*delta/epsilon and initial half-chord 4*delta/epsilon. Then t_k=(8k-4)*delta/epsilon<Tcal/epsilon but k-1>M velocities all meet the speed alternative of the printed union.
problems.result: The deterministic count is false. The counterexample family has strict margins; finite neighborhoods preserve the count violation. No estimate of their mass relative to the lemma's exponential upper bound is claimed.
counterevidence: The rendered original confirms a union, ruling out OCR substitution.
The acquired reference arXiv:1111.5843v2 uses an intersection on p.28 (Lemma 4.2, starting p.27), supporting a typographical origin and valid intended geometry.
An implicit both-conditions interpretation corrects the displayed definition rather than validating its literal union.
A bounded correction search found no separate notice for this equation; journal/unpublished correction status remains unknown.
problems.core_dependency: Lemma 9.5 is the stochastic-cycle modification supporting Proposition 9.1; the latter is explicitly used in (10.4), then (10.6), then the iteration (12.3) for Theorem 1.2.
problems.severity_reason: A demonstrated invalid derivation closely tied to the core L-infinity remainder estimate; local repair and survival of the theorem are recorded separately.

repair.statement: Replace union by intersection. A uniform interior tangent ball gives t_b>=2*r*eta^3/epsilon. Include m=0 in the combinatorial sum; a=max(1,total diffuse mass), b<=C*eta. Then I_k<=(M+1)(k*a)^M*b^(k-1-M). Choose k-1>=16(M+1), eta=c*Tcal^(-1/12), and sufficiently small fixed c; I_k<=2^(-cprime*Tcal^(5/4)).
repair.boundaries: Restores geometric count and tail scaling with constants depending on fixed domain/Gaussian parameters. Does not certify all PDE estimates or author adoption.

independent_verification.claim_fidelity: Source p.60 (9.17) actually uses union. Definitions on p.59 and Theorem 1.2 / (1.14) permit the ball, constant wall temperature and the constructed nonzero transversal velocities.
independent_verification.independent_argument: With |v|^2=1/4 and x.v=delta, |x-sv|^2-1=-2s delta+s^2/4, so s=8delta. The initial midpoint has squared norm 1-4delta^2 and exits after 4delta/epsilon. Since delta<=T/(16k), epsilon*t_k=(8k-4)delta<T/2<T while all k-1>M velocities satisfy the speed branch. This refutes the deterministic count, not the integral tail theorem.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The earlier reference's intersection and lower bound were read directly. A typographical origin and survival of the intended method are accepted and already stated.
independent_verification.repair_verification: For the intersection, the uniform interior-ball bound gives each good flight at least 2r eta^3/epsilon. With b<=C eta<1, a>=1, and k-1>=16(M+1), the inclusive sum m=0..M is at most (M+1)(ka)^M b^(k-1-M) <= (M+1)(C'T eta^12)^M. eta=c T^(-1/12) and C'c^12<=1/4 give 2^-M with M comparable to T^(5/4). Constants remain independent of epsilon and T. No whole-PDE repair is certified.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_grade: The source explicitly calls the lemma the key modification in Proposition 9.1; (10.4) uses that proposition, (10.6) combines it, and (12.3) uses the latter. Major applies to this invalid core derivation under the stated calibration despite the local repair. No main-theorem falsity is claimed.

additional_checks.check: Exact centered-Gaussian moment E[V_i^2*(|V|^2-5T)^2]=10T^3; multiplying by rho=P/T and 2/(4T^2) gives 5P.

unpromoted_candidates.reason: The compact velocity support of the auxiliary cutoff is a justified alternate reading of a collision lower bound; no global assertion is refuted here.
Normalization ambiguity was not resolved into a counterexample satisfying all hypotheses; not graded as a finding.
